subject: ui
summary: Technical details of how the theme cascade translates to CSS. For the conceptual model, see Architecture (`architecture.md`).

purpose.intro: Technical details of how the theme cascade translates to CSS. For the conceptual model, see Architecture (`architecture.md`).

reference.statement: Two attributes, never on the same node:

snippets.code:
<div element="surface--card">        element = {family}--{element}
<div layout="left-sidebar">          layout = bare name (no prefix)
snippets.caption: html

claims.text: Rules: only emit CSS for `part` values **explicitly declared** in the theme under that surface's `parts` field. An undeclared `part` is inert — zero CSS emitted. This prevents developers from using `part` as a free styling escape hatch. `part` is never used on the same node as `element` or `layout`.

reference.statement: `part="name"` marks a structural sub-region of a themed ancestor. Use it on plain divs that a designer needs to control (padding, gap, background) without giving the div a full element identity.

snippets.code:
<div element="surface--card">
  <div part="body">      ← designer controls interior here
  <div part="actions">   ← designer controls gap here
snippets.caption: html

reference.statement: Layout uses `layout="value"` directly — no family prefix.

reference.topic: Selector Model › Axis attributes (bare, no data- prefix)

reference.statement: CSS source order + specificity handles cascade priority. No variable chains or bridge systems. The engine emits rules in this order:

snippets.code:
[element^="surface--"]                                  L2 family (lowest)
[element="surface--card"]                               L3 element
[element="surface--card"][emphasis="primary"]            axis (emphasis first)
[element="surface--card"][status="error"]                axis (status later = wins)
[element="surface--card"]:hover                         pseudo-class (highest)
[element="surface--card"][emphasis="primary"]:hover      compound (most specific)
[concept="X"] [element="surface--card"]                 concept (2 selectors)
[element="A"] [element="B"]                             contextual (2 selectors)

claims.text: Everything else is plain CSS. Padding, radius, shadow, cursor, transition, typography — set directly, no variables.

reference.statement: 5 CSS custom properties handle cross-property composition:

imagesAndDiagrams.value:
| Variable | Why it exists |
|----------|---------------|
| `--bg` | Tint mixes into background via `color-mix()` |
| `--fg` | `smart-bw` computes foreground from background |
| `--tint` | One color modifies both background and border |
| `--border-color` | Tint mixes into border via `color-mix()` |
| `--bg-alpha` | Alpha composites with transparent |

snippets.caption: css

claims.text: **Zero theme = zero cascade lines.** Only structural plumbing remains.
**Only emit what the theme defines.** No defaults copied to elements.
**Deltas only.** Elements don't repeat family values.
**One file, all modes.** Default on `:root`, others on `[data-mode]`.
**Readable in devtools.** Each rule shows what it does.

Inner radius = outer radius - border-width (child sits inside parent border). For `border` mode, child extends over the border, so outer radius is used. For `rounded` mode, interior edges also get radius.
